title: Ti ricordi come sarà?
description: ‘Ti ricordi come sarà?’ (‘Do You Remember How It Will Be?’), developed in Val di Fiastra (Marche), explores territorial regeneration through participatory artistic practices. Through collaborative workshops on sewing, embroidery, and traditional wheat straw weaving, the project promoted intergenerational dialogue among the elderly—as custodians of traditional knowledge—young people, and children. Together, the participants created flags using donated bridal trousseau fabrics, featuring motifs that embody the region’s collective memories and symbols, and crafted straw weavings, preserving traditional craft techniques and strengthening community connections.
details: The project is in collaboration with ASFO dal basso e Borgofuturo and is supported by Associazione Oltre... APS as part of the European CultureAndHealth platform.

title: Gear Up! Protest Toolkit
description: Born from the urgent need to support the Palestine solidarity movement amidst intensifying repression in Germany post-October 2023, 'Gear Up!' transforms textile work into a tool for activism and mutual aid. Through collective sewing workshops, participants co-create protest vests and kits, with a focus on physical and mental well-being during political actions. Distributed alongside practical zines on international protest tactics, these textile artifacts are designed to be worn and activated. The workshop space invites a tactile engagement, turning the preparation for demonstration into a moment of care and solidarity. By materially and symbolically 'gearing up' together, participants reimagine resistance not as a solitary burden, but as a woven network of support.
details: 'Gear Up!' is a collaboration between Miriam Poletti, abstraqt and Jona Wolf, supported by Amnesty International and Art Rights Truth - Centre for Applied Human Rights and the History of Art Department at the University of York. The project continues to grow through ongoing dialogue with activists, lawyers and journalists.
credits: All photo credits to Simona Radici.

title: A Thousand Gestures
description: Conceived as a place for interaction, ‘A Thousand Gestures’ employs textile sculpture and video to explore softness as a form of community building. Created through a participatory methodology with artists-in-residence at GlogauAIR, the work challenges traditional authorship by transforming the gallery into a site of encounter. The soft sculptures are not static objects but invitations to action; visitors are encouraged to hug, cuddle, and rest upon them, physically activating the art and leaving their imprint on the shared space. The accompanying video work weaves intimate interviews with the collaborating artists, examining the vital role of touch in sustaining personal and professional bonds. By centering these shared voices, the installation reframes touch as an active, connective force that reshapes our sense of self and our relationships with others.
details: The project was supported by Memoria Artística Chema Alvargonzalez. Thanks for the help and contribution from Aariya Talcherkar, Anji Lesourne, Bianca Durrant, Camilla Marinoni, Cassandra Paige, Cynthia Chou, Dae, Duaa Bilbeisi, Elisa Pardo Puch, Ella Brew, Florencia Galecio, Getsay, Hilal Shamsaldain, Jacqueline Huskisson, Jacopo Petenello, João Motta Guedes, Jo Watson, Josefina Vidal Díaz, Maddie Baker, Marte Conesa, Michal Častulik, Nicholas Ferguson, Nina Criswell, Raisa Desypri, Raquel Gonzalez Obregon, Shannon Castor, Sergei Kurek, Suzy Royal, Tiffany Adler, Tomas Kajurov, Valentine Bossert.

title: A Thousand Gestures: Sewing Circles
description: Serving as the participatory core of the exhibition ‘A Thousand Gestures’, a series of sewing workshops took place at GlogauAIR in Berlin between January and March 2024. The initial sessions brought artists-in-residence together to collectively shape the interactive soft sculptures for the exhibition opening. Later, the circles opened to visitors, inviting them to contribute their own stitches to the installation. The bodies gathering in these sewing sessions left a tangible trace of their presence, embedding their gestures into the fabric until the exhibition’s close. Reflecting the work’s commitment to continuous evolution, these textiles will not be discarded but repurposed for future projects. They carry forward the accumulated interventions of many hands, ensuring the artwork remains a living, growing testament to collaborative creation.
details: Workshops presented at GlogauAIR Project Space in Berlin. Part of 'A Thousand Gestures', an exhibition and public programme curated by Suzy Royal. The project was supported by Memoria Artística Chema Alvargonzalez.

title: Nest: Sewing Circle
material: sublimation print on microfibre, polyester filling
description: This workshop invited participants to reframe the body not as a single entity separate from its context, but as a collective whole, which is constructed and transformed through constant interactions. In response to the widespread sense of isolation in society, the session fostered active collaboration as attendees wove together fabrics and materials to create a single, multi-element installation. By inviting the audience to physically interact with the nest, the piece extends the workshop’s spirit of connection, turning viewers into active participants.
details: Workshop presented on 11.11.23 at Backhaus Projects in Berlin. Part of 'Objects of Care', an exhibition and public programme curated by Astro collective.

title: Shoulder to Shoulder
material: sublimation print on microfibre, polyester filling
description: During the participatory workshop 'Shoulder to Shoulder', art workers living in Helsinki had the opportunity to connect the threads of their personal experiences regarding the precarity, mental health challenges, and isolation inherent in the contemporary art field. Organized in partnership with Dare to Care collective — an initiative dedicated to exposing the structural roots of these issues — the session transformed a sewing circle into a space to share strategies of resistance and support. This hands-on collaboration allowed artists Cynthia Blanchette, Ania Duldiier, Jon Dunn, Moe Louanjli, Ines Montalvao, Mathilde Palenius, Cami Ruohonen, and Kamila Śladowska to co-create the artworks for the exhibition ‘On the Texture of Feelings’ held at Myymälä2 Gallery.
details: Workshop presented on 28.06.23 at Töölö library in Helsinki. Part of 'On the Texture of Feelings', an exhibition and public programme hosted by Myymälä2 Gallery and curated by Dare to Care collective. The project was supported by Culture Moves Europe, funded by the European Union and implemented by the Goethe-Institut, and TelepART Mobility Support, run by the Finnish Cultural and Research Institutes.

title: Screens * Scream * Sex - On Pleasure
material: sublimation print on microfiber, polyester filling
description: Created for the performance by Isadora Alves, Salphinah Savin, Catherin Schöberl, and Emilymary Whitaker, this project centers on a series of custom wearable sculptures that redefine the performers' physical presence on stage. These costumes serve as extensions of the body, crafted from sublimated microfiber and polyester filling to resemble skin and fragmented body parts. The work deliberately blurs the boundaries of the individual form, making it unclear where one body ends and another begins. This visual ambiguity mirrors the performance’s exploration of collective intimacy, where choreographies are driven by recorded interviews about personal experiences of pleasure. The costumes serve as the primary medium through which the theme of skin is interrogated, transforming the performers into a fluid, interconnected entity during the presentation at Zentralwäscherei, Zürich.
details: 'Screens*Scream*Sex - On Pleasure' (50 min, English) by Isadora Alves, Salphinah Savin, Catherin Schöberl und Emilymary Whitaker presented on 24.03.23 at Zentralwäscherei, Zürich, Switzerland.
credits: All photo credits to Giovanna León.

title: Screens * Scream * Sex - Public Rehearsal
material: sublimation print on microfiber, polyester filling
description: As part of 'The Nights of the Smiling Moons' at the Fondation Beyeler, interactive and participatory public rehearsals of the performance 'Screens*Scream*Sex' were held. The costumes designed for the performers Isadora Alves, Salphinah Savin, Catherin Schöberl and Emilymary Whitaker served as the visual focal point of the audience’s exploration of pleasure and movement. The sculptures encouraged participants to engage with the concept of collective intimacy, physically manifesting the work’s core inquiry: how bodies relate, merge, and find pleasure through shared, (un)guided motion.
details: 'Screens*Scream*Sex - Public Rehearsal' (25 min, English) by Isadora Alves, Salphinah Savin, Catherin Schöberl und Emilymary Whitaker presented on 14.04.23 at Fondation Beyeler, Riehen, Switzerland.
credits: All photo credits to Giovanna León.

title: Embrace The Melting Times
description: Created in response to the social isolation exacerbated by the Covid-19 pandemic, this video work reimagines the body as a liquid, adaptive force. The narrative follows a protagonist who discovers happiness in mutation, celebrating the transformation from a rigid, constrained form into an amorphous, flowing existence. Through a blend of autobiographical and fictional elements, the piece chronicles the daily challenges of this new form — navigating rain, drinking, dripping, and slipping — as metaphors for emotional fluidity. The accompanying soundscape, a distorted and muffled field recording, immerses the viewer in an underwater sensation. The piece illustrates that embracing change and dissolving rigid boundaries is a vital strategy for survival and connection in times of isolation.

title: A Moment of Greatest Proximity and Greatest Distance
description: Created for Nouvelle Collection Paris, this project features a series of wearable sculptures that reproduce the artist’s own silhouette at a 1:1 scale. Crafted from acrylic enamel on PVC, these pieces function as artificial skins. The work directly addresses the tension between closeness and separation: while the sculptures are exact replicas of a specific body, they remain empty until activated by another. The core of the piece lies in the collaborative encounter between the object and the wearer. Models are given complete autonomy to decide how to touch, hold, and wear the sculptures. The nature of the encounter is defined by the physical negotiation between the wearer’s body and the artist’s cast. By requiring this active participation to complete the work, the piece highlights how true proximity is achieved not just through physical presence, but through the shared agency of touch and movement.
details: The project has been developed in collaboration with Nouvelle Collection Paris, curated by Sarah Nefissa Belhadjali, and presented at MO.CO. La Panacée, Montpellier, France.
credits: Photography: Alex Huanfa Cheng, Romain Moncet.
